Jet A, SAF/Jet A blends, and potential future 100% SAF fuels are subjected to the same handling and use requirements as dictated by state and federal codes. As stated in Section 2.1.3, blending SAF and Jet A occurs upstream of airports at terminals. Therefore, handling SAF/Jet A blends is a business-as-usual scenario at airports, where the same pipelines and trucks that deliver Jet A to airports are used to deliver SAF/Jet A blends. The flow rates for the pipeline from the terminal to the airports and from either the fuel hydrant system or refueling trucks to the aircraft wing are the same for both Jet A and Jet A/SAF blends. Any future 100% SAF fuels would be handled the same way and experience the same flow rates as Jet A. 40 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. In the future, drop-in fuels with 100% SAF composition could be delivered to airports in the same pipelines and trucks that deliver Jet A today due to strict fuel quality properties adopted in ASTM D7566 and the assumption that it would be incorporated into ASTM D1655. The emergency procedures for fuel leaks and dumping fuel are the same for Jet A and SAF/Jet A blends. No changes to emergency operations and procedures are anticipated for a future 100% SAF fuel adhering to strict fuel quality properties. 41 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies at www.nlr.gov/publications. 3 Alternative Liquid Hydrocarbon Chemistries Jet X is a term used to refer to various alternative liquid hydrocarbon chemistries. Jet X can be defined as non-drop-in liquid hydrocarbon synthetic aviation turbine fuels. “Non-drop-in” is defined as fuels that do not meet ASTM D1655 or ASTM D7566. The motivation for investigating Jet X fuels is due to potential properties that could increase fuel economy, improve local air quality around airports, and reduce contrail formation. These fuels are in the early stages of research and could include high iso-alkanes/cycloalkanes, and fuels would have no or low aromatics.
